metadata.title: Panitumumab 6mg/kg and FOLFIRI Therapy -14 day
metadata.indication: First- or second-line treatment of adult patients with wild-type RAS metastatic colorectal cancer as specified by NCCP.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

metadata.schedule_summary: A 14-day cycle: panitumumab, irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil start on Day 1, followed by a fluorouracil pump for about 46 hours. Arrange disconnection around Day 3. Continue according to benefit and tolerance.

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: The treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Any dose modification should be discussed with a Consultant.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Source-mapped NCCP 00448 v5; independent clinical/pharmacy validation remains pending. Use the current source and individual clinical judgement.

indications.description: First-line treatment of adult patients with wild-type RAS metastatic colorectal cancer.
Second-line treatment of wild-type RAS metastatic colorectal cancer after first-line fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy excluding irinotecan.
First- or second-line RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer.

rule_engine.conflict_policy: Use the most restrictive overall action; combine component changes using the greatest reduction per component rather than summing reductions.

diarrhoea_current_grade.label: Current diarrhoea grade
diarrhoea_current_grade.assessment_guidance: Count stools per day above the patient's baseline, assess ostomy output, continence, hydration, fever, abdominal pain, haemodynamic compromise and whether hospital care is indicated.

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No increase above the patient's usual stool frequency or ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Increase of fewer than 4 stools per day above baseline, or mild increase in ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Increase of 4–6 stools per day above baseline, or moderate increase in ostomy output; limits instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Increase of 7 or more stools per day above baseline, incontinence, hospital care indicated, or severe ostomy-output increase; limits self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

rash_grade.label: Current panitumumab skin toxicity grade
rash_grade.assessment_guidance: Grade the dermatological reaction clinically, not acne alone. Record the number of severe episodes and response after withholding. Blistering, skin detachment or infection requires urgent assessment.

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No acneiform rash.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Papules/pustules covering under 10% body-surface area, with or without pruritus or tenderness.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Papules/pustules covering 10-30% body-surface area with or without symptoms and psychosocial/instrumental-ADL impact, or over 30% with mild symptoms.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Papules/pustules covering over 30% body-surface area with moderate/severe symptoms, limiting self-care ADL, or local superinfection requiring oral antibiotics.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences, or extensive superinfection requiring IV antibiotics.

infusion_reaction_grade.label: Infusion reaction grade
infusion_reaction_grade.assessment_guidance: Document timing, symptoms, need to interrupt treatment, response to symptomatic therapy, recurrence, hospitalisation and any airway or haemodynamic compromise.

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No infusion-related or hypersensitivity reaction.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Mild transient reaction; interruption of the infusion is not indicated; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Infusion interruption or treatment is indicated, with prompt response to symptomatic medication; prophylaxis may be needed for 24 hours or less.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Prolonged symptoms not rapidly responsive to treatment/brief interruption, or recurrence after initial improvement; hospitalisation indicated for clinical sequelae.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

supportive_care.mapping_basis: Panitumumab is low risk; the chemotherapy combination is driven by irinotecan, which is moderate risk (NCCP V6 table 7).
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for moderate emetogenic risk
supportive_care.premedication: Not routinely required for panitumumab; local policy after reactions. Chemotherapy antiemetics follow NCCP/local regimen risk.
other_supportive_care: Pre-emptive skin care, sun protection and prescribed therapy under local EGFR policy.
Monitor magnesium, calcium and potassium before/during treatment and for up to 8 weeks after; NCCP specifies monthly electrolytes for 2 months post treatment.
Review eye symptoms, lung symptoms, skin infection and diarrhoea; give urgent contact plan.
NCCP prophylactic atropine 250 micrograms SC; assess contraindications including glaucoma. Give a separate delayed-diarrhoea plan.

monitoring: Validated extended RAS wild-type result and exact first-/second-line indication; review prior irinotecan exposure.
FBC, renal and liver profile; DPD test before fluorouracil. Renal impairment can confound uracil-based testing.
Baseline electrolytes, magnesium and calcium; bowel function, obstruction risk, skin, lung symptoms, medication interactions and pump readiness. ECG if cardiac function is compromised.
FBC, renal and liver profile before each cycle. Review early and delayed diarrhoea separately, hydration, fever, mouth soreness and skin/eye/respiratory symptoms.
Check magnesium/calcium/potassium and correct abnormalities according to the local EGFR monitoring plan.
Monthly electrolytes, magnesium and calcium for two months after the last panitumumab dose.
Disease assessment follows the consultant plan. Escalate persistent diarrhoea, fever or dehydration between visits. Check INR if taking warfarin, as clinically indicated.
